rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a Day-5 expanded blastocyst and appropriately notes limits of a single still image, but includes speculative details (collapse, two images, granular spots) and only moderate precision on ICM/TE/zona assessment.
Integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, male factor, prior ectopic/biochemical history, sperm parameters, and endometrial thickness well, with reasonable linkage to prognosis and transfer planning.

Overall logic is mostly sound, but there are internal inconsistencies and hedging (e.g., varying implantation ranges, comments about fresh/frozen timing, and some speculative concerns) that weaken coherence.

Largely aligned with IVF practice: recognizes 3AA as high quality, supports single embryo transfer in a young patient, and appropriately flags hydrosalpinx/tubal evaluation after ectopic history. Minor deviations include overemphasis on bed rest/alcohol advice and some speculative PGT-A discussion.

Provides useful next steps such as single embryo transfer, review of tubal status/hydrosalpinx, cavity evaluation if failures continue, and consideration of sperm DNA fragmentation or recurrent loss workup. Some recommendations remain somewhat generic.
